content: 1. Amifampridine has the potential to induce seizures. The risk of seizures may increase when co-administered with drugs that lower the seizure threshold. 2. Amitriptyline and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 3. Amoxapine and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 4. Arformoterol and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 5. Aripiprazole and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 6. Co-administration of levofloxacin with artemether/lumefantrine increases the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 7. Atomoxetine and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 8. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Levofloxacin and bedaquiline both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring, including ECG, is recommended. 10. Betamethasone and levofloxacin both increase the risk of other adverse effects (see comment). Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Co-administration of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids may increase the risk of tendon rupture. 11. Buprenorphine (transdermal) and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 12. Calcium acetate and levofloxacin can decrease each other's levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution, monitor the patient, and separate administration by at least 2 hours. 13. Calcium carbonate and levofloxacin can decrease each other's levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution, monitor the patient, and separate administration by at least 2 hours. 14. Calcium chloride and levofloxacin can decrease each other's levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution, monitor the patient, and separate administration by at least 2 hours. 15. Calcium citrate and levofloxacin can decrease each other's levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution, monitor the patient, and separate administration by at least 2 hours. 16. Calcium gluconate and levofloxacin can decrease each other's levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution, monitor the patient, and separate administration by at least 2 hours. 17. Levofloxacin and celecoxib may increase the risk of central nervous system (CNS) stimulation or seizures. The mechanism involves displacement of GABA from its receptors in the brain. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 18. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of levofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 19. Chlorpromazine and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 20. Levofloxacin and citalopram both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. ECG monitoring is recommended, especially when co-administered with other QT-prolonging drugs. 21. Clarithromycin and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 22. Clomipramine and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 23. Clozapine and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 24. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Corticotropin and levofloxacin both increase the risk of other adverse effects (see comment). Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Co-administration of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids may increase the risk of tendon rupture. 26. Cortisone and levofloxacin both increase the risk of other adverse effects (see comment). Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Co-administration of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids may increase the risk of tendon rupture. 27. Crizotinib and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. ECG monitoring is recommended, especially when co-administered with other QT-prolonging drugs. 28. Crofelemer increases the levels of levofloxacin by inhibiting transporters such as MRP2 and OATP1A2 in the gut. However, systemic inhibition is unlikely due to minimal absorption of crofelemer. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 29. Dasatinib and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 30. Degarelix and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 31. Desipramine and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 32. Deutetrabenazine and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically significant extent. However, certain conditions may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death when using QT-prolonging drugs (e.g., bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, co-administration with other QT-prolonging drugs, or congenital QT prolongation). 33. Dexamethasone and levofloxacin both increase the risk of other adverse effects (see comment). Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Co-administration of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids may increase the risk of tendon rupture. 34. Levofloxacin and diclofenac may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures. The mechanism involves displacement of GABA from its receptors in the brain. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended.
